# Results

See [Powerpoint](
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1WN1psDLrEdPYpBb7KLWSUh0Jw6ZX2HDJ?rtpof=true&usp=drive_fs) presentation, results as of October 31.

Results pertaining to trends in PNI and total spawners among management strategies are generally consistent across population scenarios (Figure \@ref(fig:pf)).

The choice of pNOB target strongly influences PNI with higher PNI from higher pNOB (Figure \@ref(fig:dt-pni)).
With pNOB target of 1, the median PNI can exceed 0.5 in all scenarios indicative of an "integrated-transition" biological designation defined by @withler2018 for enhanced populations. 

Higher in-river exploitation rates leads to lower spawner numbers in the long-term with larger removals from the system.
Higher in-river exploitation rates slightly increase PNI, but the effect is marginal to almost negligible.

Increases in freshwater survival (comparing among scenarios A-C) or lower marine ER (comparing A and D) increases both spawner numbers and PNI. 
With declining fecundity, there are fewer spawners due to reduced egg production with a marginal decrease in PNI, comparing scenario A and E.
Changes in PNI are frequently more marginal in scenarios D and E because the differences in survival and fecundity impact NOS and HOS equally.

Selection of a management strategy that meets objectives, e.g., maximize spawners and PNI, can be facilitated by comparing management choices in a tradeoff figure (Figure \@ref(fig:dt-tradeoff)). 
The strategy that maximizes both objectives are in the top right corner for each scenario. None of the evaluated strategies are clearly optimal for maximizing both spawners and PNI in all scenarios. 
In such a case, it is helpful to first prioritize either objective, high PNI or high spawners, to filter the management strategies that perform well for the primary objective. 
The management strategy among the filtered choices that performs best for the secondary objective can then be chosen.
For example, if maximizing spawners is the primary objective, then an in-river exploitation rate of 0.5 should be used, with three candidate pNOB targets to choose from.
Maximizing PNI, the secondary objective, is always achieved with pNOB of 1 in all scenarios.

(ref:fig-pf) Table of performance measures reporting outcomes at the end of the projection for 9 management options (1-9, rows), with primary metrics left of the dashed vertical black line. Each panel represents outcomes by scenario (A-E). Each column is colour-coded with magenta representing zero, green the maximium value of each metric, and white representing half of the maximum. Total spawners, Brood, ESSR catch, and escapement are in units of abundance (> 0), mean age is in units of years (between 2--5), egg production is in millions, hatchery releases in hundreds of thousands, and all others are proportions/probabilities between 0--1. Table cells report medians for all metrics the probability-based metrics (prefixed with P_). Medians are calculated across 100 stochastic simulations, and may not be directly comparable across columns.

```
